skill.name: sragent
skill.description: Query SRA and GEO, convert accessions, analyze genomics metadata, identify sequencing technologies, and retrieve associated publications with the SRAgent toolkit.
skill.summary: Investigate SRA and GEO datasets, metadata, technologies, and linked publications.
skill.author: ArcInstitute

security_audit.summary: Most matches are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, official URLs, placeholder credentials, and legitimate scientific database queries. Confirmed risks include secret disclosure, mutable source installation, predictable temporary files, command-line credentials, and silent file overwrite. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting commands reveal credential values and .env contents.
remediation.suggestion: Use presence-only checks that return SET or UNSET, and redact all secret values from terminal output, logs, and agent context.

remediation.issue: The skill tells the agent to request secret environment-variable values from users.
remediation.suggestion: Never request credential values in chat. Direct users to configure secrets locally through a secure environment or credential manager.

remediation.issue: CORE_API_KEY is passed as a command-line argument.
remediation.suggestion: Read the key from the environment or a protected credential source so it does not appear in the process argument list.

remediation.issue: Installation uses an unpinned repository checkout and executes package build code.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an immutable commit or signed release, verify integrity, and require explicit user approval before cloning or installing.

remediation.issue: Examples use predictable shared temporary filenames.
remediation.suggestion: Create temporary files with mktemp, restrict permissions, quote paths, and remove files with a cleanup trap.

remediation.issue: A batch example silently overwrites accessions.csv.
remediation.suggestion: Create a unique output file or check for an existing file and obtain user confirmation before replacement.

content.user_title: Investigate SRA and GEO Genomics Datasets
content.value_statement: Genomics dataset investigation often requires multiple accession, metadata, and literature searches. SRAgent coordinates SRA and GEO queries, technology identification, and publication retrieval.
actual_capabilities: Convert GSE, SRP, PRJNA, SRX, and ERX accessions to related experiment or run identifiers.
Query NCBI Entrez for dataset summaries, accession links, and associated publications.
Analyze SRA and GEO metadata, including organism, platform, assay, and library preparation.
Use BigQuery-backed workflows for batch metadata analysis when Google Cloud credentials are available.
Identify single-cell status and common RNA sequencing technologies from metadata and publications.
Retrieve available manuscripts and enrich CSV inputs with PubMed identifiers, DOIs, and download paths.
limitations: The SRAgent package and Python 3.11 or later must be installed separately.
Model queries require a provider key, while BigQuery and optional sources require separate credentials.
Publication retrieval depends on network access, source availability, and open-access permissions.
Users must verify metadata interpretations and scientific conclusions against primary records and publications.

use_cases.title: Triage a sequencing experiment
use_cases.description: Summarize an accession, identify its organism and technology, and locate linked publications before selecting data for analysis.

use_cases.title: Map accession hierarchies
use_cases.description: Convert study identifiers into experiment and run accessions for reproducible pipelines and sample inventories.

use_cases.title: Curate dataset literature
use_cases.description: Retrieve papers for accession lists and add PubMed identifiers, DOIs, and local download paths to a CSV.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize one experiment
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize SRA experiment [SRX accession]. Report organism, platform, library strategy, single-cell status, and linked publications. Cite the accession for each result.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one known experiment

prompt_templates.title: Convert a study accession
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert [GSE or PRJNA accession] to related SRX and SRR accessions. Present the hierarchy and note unresolved links.
prompt_templates.scenario: Build an accession map for a study

prompt_templates.title: Compare sequencing experiments
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [accession A] and [accession B] by organism, assay, platform, library preparation, read layout, and single-cell technology. Flag missing metadata.
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluate two experiments for downstream analysis

prompt_templates.title: Process a publication batch
prompt_templates.prompt: Process [CSV path] using column [column name]. Retrieve metadata and open publications, limit concurrency to [number], and summarize failures without exposing credentials.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced batch curation with controlled network use

output: Linked publications: PubMed and DOI references when available

output_examples.input: Convert GSE121737 to experiment and run accessions.
output_examples.output: A hierarchy lists the GEO series, linked SRA study, experiment accessions, and run accessions. Missing links are labeled for review.
A publication summary lists discovered PubMed identifiers, DOIs, source availability, download status, and destination paths.

best_practices: Verify returned accessions against NCBI records before downstream analysis.
Use minimal concurrency and follow each provider's rate limits and access terms.
Keep credentials in protected environment storage and redact them from prompts, logs, and command arguments.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys or .env contents into chat, commands, or logs.
Do not treat missing metadata as proof that a sequencing technology was not used.
Do not start large downloads without reviewing storage, concurrency, and source access terms.

faq.question: What must be installed before using this skill?
faq.answer: Install SRAgent with Python 3.11 or later. Configure one supported model provider before running agent-backed queries.

faq.question: Can it work without Google BigQuery?
faq.answer: Yes. Entrez queries and paper retrieval remain available, while BigQuery-dependent analysis is skipped.

faq.question: Which accession formats are supported?
faq.answer: The documented workflows cover GSE, GSM, SRP, PRJNA, SRX, ERX, SRR, ERR, ERP, and PRJEB identifiers.

faq.question: Can it download every linked publication?
faq.answer: No. Downloads depend on valid links, source availability, network access, and open-access permissions.

faq.question: Does it support batch processing?
faq.answer: Yes. CSV inputs can be processed for metadata and publications, with configurable accession columns and concurrency.

faq.question: Should I trust every metadata interpretation?
faq.answer: No. Verify important fields and scientific conclusions against NCBI records and the primary publications.
